content.overview: Hofburg Palace Vienna conference center - The Hofburg Vienna holds 17,000 m² of space in 35 rooms for events ranging from 50 to 4,900 persons. The heart of the property is embodied by the imperial staterooms which are equipped with ultramodern event technology.
content.complex_details: Altogether, the entire Hofburg complex (the former winter residence of the Habsburgs) contains a total area of 500,000 m² on 18 wings with 54 staircases, 19 courtyards and 2,600 different rooms. The Hofburg is proud to serve as the home address for following important institutions.

destination_vienna.description: Vienna: one of the most popular congress cities in the world, a home to one of four major United Nations offices, world music capital, business and financial centre, cultural interface. And everyone who meets at the Hofburg cannot resiste to Vienna's charms.
destination_vienna.location: The Hofburg Vienna is situated in direct proximity to some of Vienna's most famous sights as well as the shopping districts, hotels and restaurants of Vienna's Old Town.

swiss_wing.description: The oldest sector, dating from the 13th century, forms the Swiss Courtyard.
features: The Burgkapelle (Imperial Chapel), a Gothic chapel from the 15th century
Rittersaal (Knight's Hall), where Empress Maria Theresa was baptized (15 May 1717)

neue_burg_wing.construction: Constructed between 1881 and 1913 as part of the (never-completed) Kaiserforum project

content.summary: The Hofburg Palace stands as a testament to the Habsburg dynasty's martial, cultural, and political legacy. Its diverse architectural phases—from medieval fortifications and Gothic chapels to Renaissance palaces and Baroque halls—mirror over 700 years of Austrian history. Today, the palace remains a vibrant hub, housing state institutions, museums, cultural venues, and international organizations, while continuing its centuries-old role as a stage for national heritage and diplomacy.
